# Hunspell compiler golden

`hunspell_controlled.dic` is generated by official Hunspell `substrings.pl`,
not by the benchmark converter or by this repository's hyphenator.

- Upstream script: <https://github.com/hunspell/hyphen/blob/0d69357820f1fe0d79a1e7705a8a7a07b2968a97/substrings.pl>
- Script SHA-256: `6256b1b0a3d912be8e0337a26bded5b0a11a97332a891f44af4b6258f44beb41`
- Input: the 4939 newline-separated tokens returned by `controlledPatternTokens()`, followed by one newline. The duplicate `.ri4g` is retained. No exceptions.
- Input SHA-256: `42c331cff74ac14cbcbd9704dec150c0642f48497658e49c83a977a8c0a19420`
- Invocation: `perl substrings.pl controlled_patterns.txt upstream_controlled.dic UTF-8 3 3`
- Normalization: retain the first three header lines, lexicographically sort all 6400 remaining pattern records, and terminate each line with LF.
- Normalized golden SHA-256: `178516f759dab34e020bc6a8f69c11e449eda86c27d048a1a1962fa75d2f8a46`

The regression compares every normalized generated record to this independent
fixture. A separate small hand-calculated prefix/suffix-overlap golden validates
why copying raw TeX rules directly into a Hunspell dictionary is insufficient.
The full-corpus agreement check is additional regression coverage, not an oracle.

Rules retain the source pattern licensing documented in `../../assets/README.md`.
The upstream script is not vendored or required at benchmark runtime.
